entry.title: me
entry.content:
i am not an outdoorsmen. not an engineer. not a weightlifter. not a musician, pianist or singer. not an artist. not a cook

i strive to be the embodiment of free expression. no ego. just a being of with access to human experience. a spectator to the experiential qualities of reality i invite everyone else to do the same.

i will never stop thinking. i will never stop being a thinker. just need to alchemize it into some productive

entry.title: toy story
entry.content:
toy story and the spirit of thrifting

wabi-sabi https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HdThVCKzn20

our world is plagued by unused pens and pencils. markers and erasers.

remnants of a bygone era

rummaging through my old stuff has sort of reinvigorated my childhood spirit

i have become such a pussy

my old self would not approve

its only fair that i honor my old self’s intentions of preserving history by doing everything in my power to archive my documents as nicely as possible

entry.title: fishiness
entry.content:
fishiness is flavor. fat is flavor.

its potency. many cultures shy away from it. the ones that don’t have the best food, imo

what does that say about the world at large?

fermentation, depth and complexity, nuance

perhaps the most interesting and richest ideas are the most pungent, the most funky

entry.title: intellectualism
entry.content:
is understanding and the illusion of it one and the same?

how much of language truly encodes meaning?

if ai hallucinations can produce 50% accuracy in conveying true meaning, what is the distinction of ai between “true human thought”

the reality of the usefulness of thought is that it only has to be a certain percentage “correct” to be “useful”

what percentage of an info’s accuracy and precision the factor that skews understanding and perception? maybe it’s highly dependent on what domain. but sometimes the overarching concept is more important than the granular numbers and details
entry.summary: is understanding and the illusion of it one and the same?

entry.title: ai
entry.content:
the topic of ai is so overplayed and redundant. not another pseudo-intellectual thought should ever be uttered about it again. in any case, here’s my opinions/thoughts on the matter.

ai taken to its natural/ultimate conclusion holds significance of mythical proportions. i remember when the classic question of ‘if you were granted one wish, what would it be?’ my friend answered some kind of entity (perhaps robotc in construction) that could perhaps answer any question about the universe and its origin. ai has the potential to become this learning companian of mythic proportions, able to answer any question you throw at it.

its simultaneously awe-inspiring and a bit terrifying. recreating God-like sentient capability

entry.title: home
entry.content:
When we physically occupy a space for enough time, do we eventually spiritually occupy a space, calling it home? Where does this adaptation come from? The way we lay our imprint on the space physically? What makes a space more homely. No matter how dicrepid and disgusting the place, do humans have the innate ability to call anywhere home?

can we mold our soul and spirit to conform to/occupy any physical space in harmony? do humans possess that innate ability, some requiring more work to draw that out of them?

this thought was spurred by my experience living at UCLA. i have lived in a plethora living arrangements during my time, ranging from pretty nice to putrid/disgusting. yet with each place, provided some settling time, i have been able to reach a comparable level of physical and emotional comfort each time.

perhaps that speaks to my natural ability to adapt lol? i guess these changes truly aren’t that dramatic, and i am just hyperbolizing the whole topic.
entry.summary: When we physically occupy a space for enough time, do we eventually spiritually occupy a space, calling it home? Where does this adaptation come from? The way we lay our imprint on the space physically? What makes a space more homely. No matter how dicrepid and disgusting the place, do humans have the innate ability to call anywhere home?
